extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors preparing and submitting e-prints to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and acceptance criteria for preparing and submitting scholarly manuscripts and associated files to the arXiv e-print repository, including format, metadata, timing, and moderation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical and refereeable scientific contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv should be topical and refereeable scientific contributions that follow accepted standards of scholarly communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material must be scientific and appropriate to arXiv categories; follow scholarly norms for content and presentation so it is discoverable and suitable for the repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered authors only
rubrics_metrics.description: We only accept submissions from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a new user or are submitting to a new category, you may be required to find endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation for appropriateness and topicality
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are subject to a moderation process that verifies material is appropriate and topical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material that contains offensive language, non-scientific content, or is plagiarized may be removed. Moderation may delay or prevent announcement if standards are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to distribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must grant arXiv.org an irrevocable license to distribute the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting this license is required for submission; consult Submission Terms and Agreement for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to submission terms and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must agree to the Submission Terms and Agreement and Instructions for Submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of these terms is mandatory before completing a submission; follow the linked instructions for procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-submission expected; third-party restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to self-submit. Submissions by a third party are only accepted under limited conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See instructions for third-party submissions and index submissions for conference proceedings to learn allowed workflows and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for availability (submission schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: New submissions received by 14:00 (Eastern Daylight/Standard Time Zone) are generally made available at 20:00 (Eastern) based on the schedule for availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits and final submission before 14:00 Monday–Friday will not delay announcement. Check the schedule of availability and local time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission formats for text (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted submission formats (in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX, PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is to store articles in portable, stable formats; LaTeX/TeX are preferred. Note: “We do not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source, and we do not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.” Full-text HTML is no longer accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure formats and processing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure formats: PostScript (PS, EPS) — requires LaTeX processing; JPEG, GIF, PNG or PDF figures — requires PDFLaTeX processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit with omitted figures (external links to figures are not accepted). If submitting figures with LaTeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., graphics and graphicx) so figures appear in the document. arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: No omitted or externally linked figures
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, even if you provide links to view figures externally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures that are part of the article must be included in the submission files themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File names that contain other characters (e.g., spaces, question marks, asterisks) will be rejected. These restrictions ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name and extension case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on our system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same. Ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX include commands) match case exactly regardless of local OS behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of ancillary files and data sets
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) that are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files for permitted formats, size limits, and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: See separate instructions for preparing the title and abstract for inclusion in metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title and abstract are used on abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching; prepare them carefully and follow metadata instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and correct before final submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the final 'Submit Article' step, be sure to carefully check the title and abstract (metadata) and the processed files, and correct any errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact arXiv administrators for help if needed. Only complete the final submit step when satisfied with metadata and processed files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit option to modify before announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, select the 'Unsubmit' icon next to the submission on your user page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting returns it to incomplete status and allows you to modify files and resubmit. Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing, replacement, and versioning behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: No additional versions are generated when edits are done before the submission is publicly announced. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Instead, replace the original submission. Authors are encouraged to update and make corrections by replacing the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support limits for TeX issues
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure use of standard macro packages and verify processing locally; arXiv will not troubleshoot TeX compilation problems for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and public submission availability information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about when submissions are made publicly available is provided on the public submission availability page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the public submission availability page and versions help pages for details on scheduling and how versions are handled.
